comparison_basis: Same incremental pre-remuneration company profit/cost budget; no numeric comparison computed.
assumptions: Illustrative Ontario resident age 40; works in and owns 100% voting control of a CCPC.
Reasonable salary for actual work versus ordinary non-eligible taxable dividend from active business profit eligible for small-business treatment.
Qualitative draft: no amounts, rates, contribution ceilings, tax winner or equivalence asserted.
CPP/RRSP salary effects use can and require headroom below annual ceilings and applicable adjustments.
Exclude capital dividends, loans, eligible dividends, refundable corporate tax and associated-company/passive-income complications.
All legal mechanisms remain pending successful current primary-source review.

claims.statement: A reasonable salary for actual work can reduce corporate taxable income.
claims.display_text: A reasonable salary for your work can reduce the company’s taxable income.
claims.note: Check business-income computation, deductibility and reasonableness; no operative provision was retrieved.

claims.statement: For the stated ordinary active-business-income scenario, a non-eligible dividend is distributed from profit after corporate income tax; the distribution is not a salary expense deduction.
claims.display_text: A dividend reaches you after company tax.
claims.note: No rates used. Excludes capital dividends and refundable-tax complications; add statutory evidence for dividend non-deductibility.

claims.statement: An ordinary taxable non-eligible dividend has shareholder income-tax treatment that includes a gross-up and dividend tax credit.
claims.display_text: Then comes your personal tax—with a dividend tax credit.
claims.note: Credit is not a claim that exact corporate tax is reimbursed or total salary/dividend tax is equal.

claims.statement: Ordinary pensionable salary can add CPP pensionable earnings and requires employee and employer contributions within applicable rules and annual ceilings.
claims.display_text: Salary can add to your CPP earnings record.
claims.note: Age 40; assume pensionable employment and earnings below applicable ceilings. No guaranteed pension increment or amount.

claims.statement: Salary included in earned income can create new RRSP room for the following year, subject to the dollar limit and adjustments.
claims.display_text: And create new RRSP room for next year.
claims.note: 2026 earned income affects 2027 room; no 2027 cap is asserted. Room is not a deposit.

claims.statement: Dividends themselves do not create CPP pensionable earnings or RRSP earned income.
claims.display_text: Dividends don’t create those new earnings or new room.
claims.note: Need separate CPP statutory/administrative evidence plus ITA 146 earned-income definition; none retrieved. Existing rights remain separate.

claims.statement: Choosing a dividend does not itself erase prior CPP earnings records or unused RRSP room.
claims.display_text: Existing records and unused room stay visible.
claims.note: Visual continuity claim, not a promise that benefits/room never change for other reasons. Obtain separate CPP support.

claims.statement: An amount comparison must start from the same company cost and include all material company and personal costs; this draft makes no cash or total-tax winner claim.
claims.display_text: Compare the same company cost—and the consequences beyond today’s cash.
claims.note: Internal comparison discipline. No primary legal authority claimed; no assertion of exact tax integration.
